candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of which species and triggering conditions activate this automatic quarterly frequency increase would change which toxicity monitoring obligations apply during Federal FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall conduct a total of three (3) additional tests for any species that demonstrates significant lethal effects at or below the critical dilution.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of 'significant lethal effects at or below the critical dilution' determines both whether a WET compliance failure occurred (Purpose A) and whether three additional retests were required (Purpose B); absent or disputed retest evidence affects missing-evidence classification (Purpose C).

candidates.exact_span: The three additional tests shall be conducted monthly during the next three consecutive months.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of when the three-month retest window begins would change which specific months in FY2025 carried a monitoring obligation.

candidates.exact_span: If testing on a quarterly basis, the permittee may substitute one of the additional tests in lieu of one routine toxicity test.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a permittee was on quarterly testing and whether substitution was permissible affects whether a given period required a separate retest or could be satisfied by routine monitoring, changing obligation status and no-data semantics.

candidates.exact_span: A full report shall be prepared for each test required by this section in accordance with the reporting requirements previously outlined and available upon request from the Agency.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of which tests require reporting and what constitutes an adequate report affects whether monitoring evidence is established or remains missing for retest events.

candidates.exact_span: If persistent lethality is demonstrated by failure of one or more retests, the permittee shall initiate Toxicity Reduction Evaluation (TRE) requirements as specified in Part 6 of this section.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of what constitutes 'persistent lethality' and 'failure of one or more retests' determines whether TRE initiation obligations were triggered during FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall notify EPA in writing within 5 days of notification of the failure of any retest, and the TRE initiation date will be the test completion date of the first failed retest.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different interpretations of the notification trigger and the TRE initiation date anchor change the timing and applicability of subsequent TRE-related obligations.

candidates.exact_span: A TRE may also be required due to a demonstration of intermittent effects at or below the critical dilution, or for failure to perform the required retests.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of 'intermittent effects at or below the critical dilution' bears on WET limit exceedance (Purpose A); failure to perform retests independently triggers TRE (Purpose B); unperformed retests are a documented no-data versus violation-versus-conditional case (Purpose C).

candidates.exact_span: A TRE is triggered following two test failures (a failure followed by one retest failure).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether an initial failure plus one retest failure occurred determines if mandatory TRE obligations attached during the evaluation period.

candidates.exact_span: Within ninety (90) days of confirming lethality in the retests, the permittee shall submit a Toxicity Reduction Evaluation (TRE) Action Plan and Schedule for conducting a TRE to the EPA WET Coordinator at 6WQ-PO.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of when lethality is 'confirmed' in the retests sets the 90-day deadline for TRE Action Plan submission and whether that obligation was due in FY2025.
